title: Numbers 9: Round Tens and a Hundred (20, 30, 40, 50, 100)
description: Meet двадцать, тридцать, сорок, пятьдесят, шестьдесят, семьдесят, восемьдесят, девяносто, сто. The round tens and one hundred all act like the numbers from five upward: the noun goes into the genitive plural.
descriptionRussian: Знакомимся с круглыми десятками и сотней: двадцать, тридцать, сорок, пятьдесят, шестьдесят, семьдесят, восемьдесят, девяносто, сто. Все они подчиняются правилу 5+: существительное в родительном падеже множественного числа.
intro: Nothing new happens to the noun today, which makes this a lesson about the numbers themselves. Two are worth flagging. Forty stands entirely alone in Russian, related to nothing else in the system. And the words for twenty and thirty sit one letter away from teen words you learned last lesson. They happen to take the same form on the noun, so a slip there costs you the number rather than the grammar. Say them side by side.
rules: Round tens and 100 all take the noun in the genitive plural. Двадцать, тридцать, сорок, пятьдесят, шестьдесят, семьдесят, восемьдесят, девяносто, сто.
Endings on the noun are the same as after 5-10: -ов on masculine hard consonants (двадцать студентов), zero on feminine -а (тридцать машин).
20 and 30 (двадцать, тридцать) use the suffix -дцать. The teen suffix -надцать (двенадцать, тринадцать) is one letter different and is a completely different number.
40 is irregular: сорок stands alone with no shared family.
Compound numbers like 21 or 25 are decided by their LAST word (preview only): двадцать пять книг follows 'пять', двадцать один брат follows 'один'. The full system belongs to a later track.
examples: В классе двадцать студентов. (Twenty students in the class.) Round ten + masculine + -ов.
У меня тридцать книг. (I have thirty books.) Round ten + feminine -а dropping.
В доме сорок комнат. (Forty rooms in the house.) Round ten + zero ending.
У Антона пятьдесят котов. (Anton has fifty cats.) Round ten + masculine + -ов.
В школе сто учеников. (One hundred pupils in the school.) Round ten + masculine + -ов.
На полке девяносто книг. (Ninety books on the shelf.) Round ten + zero ending.

tables.title: Round Tens + the Two Gen Pl Patterns

items.promptEnglish: Recap from Lesson 8: I have twelve books.
items.explanation: Recap from Lesson 8. A teen number takes the genitive plural: книг. Today, round tens follow exactly the same rule.

items.promptEnglish: There are twenty students in the class.
items.explanation: Двадцать — круглый десяток. Round tens take the gen pl, the same form 5-10 and the teens used: студент → студентов.

items.hint: Round ten → gen pl. Feminine -а drops.
items.explanation: Тридцать — круглый десяток. Feminine -а drops with the zero ending: книг. The pattern is the same one you used after пять and after одиннадцать.
Пятьдесят — круглый десяток. The -десят ending tells you this is 'five tens', which is firmly in the 5+ family. Кот → котов.

items.promptEnglish: There are forty rooms in the house.
items.hint: Round ten → gen pl. Feminine -а drops.
items.explanation: Сорок is irregular as a word but completely regular as a counting trigger: it acts like every other round ten. Комната → комнат (zero ending).

items.promptEnglish: There are one hundred pupils in the school.
items.explanation: Сто — самый простой из больших чисел. Same rule as round tens: gen pl. Ученик → учеников. Сто is the round number you will hear most often in everyday life: prices, ages, distances.

blanks: У меня девяносто _____. (I have ninety books.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Девяносто is irregular as a word but takes the standard 5+ rule: the noun is in the gen pl. Книга → книг. Same zero ending you used after пять, шесть, and the teens.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: There are twenty tables at the school.
errorCorrection.explanation: Round tens (двадцать, тридцать, сорок, пятьдесят...) all take the GENITIVE PLURAL: столов. The 5-and-up rule continues into the tens.

errorCorrection.sentence: У меня тридцать газеты на полке.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: I have thirty newspapers on the shelf.
errorCorrection.explanation: After round tens (тридцать), the noun is in the GENITIVE PLURAL: газет. The gen pl of газета is the bare stem газет (no ending, typical for fem -а nouns). Газеты is either nom pl or gen sg; the 5+ rule rules both out.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: This school has a hundred windows.
errorCorrection.explanation: Сто (one hundred) takes the GENITIVE PLURAL on the noun: окон (with the fleeting -о- inside the stem). The 5-and-up rule covers all big numbers from пять to сто.

minimalPairs.explanation: Round ten → gen pl with the zero ending: книг. The form 'книги' is the gen sg (used after 2, 3, 4). Round tens are firmly in the 5+ family.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: There are fifty students in the class.
minimalPairs.explanation: Round ten → gen pl with -ов: студентов. The form 'студента' (gen sg) would only fit after 2, 3, 4.

reviewVocab.definition: round tens (numbers with no small digit on the end: 20, 30, ... 90; all take the gen pl)
reviewVocab.example: К круглым десяткам относятся 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90. После всех этих чисел существительное стоит в родительном падеже множественного числа.

reviewVocab.definition: one hundred (the simplest large number; takes the gen pl like the round tens)
reviewVocab.example: В школе сто учеников: 'сто' требует родительного падежа множественного числа от 'ученик'.

reviewVocab.definition: compound numeral (a number built from two or more words: двадцать один, двадцать пять; the last word picks the rule, taught in detail at B1)
reviewVocab.example: Числительное 'двадцать пять' — составное: правило выбирает последнее слово 'пять', поэтому 'двадцать пять книг'.
